message.content: The contract demands exact single-rounding to FP16 across all finite inputs; the kernel uses an FP32 split form with one final cvt, so double-rounding near FP16 tie boundaries and the subnormal/underflow tail are the prime failure surfaces. I'll record these as concrete in-scope claims.

function.arguments: {"rationale": "libdevice.exp has ~1 ulp FP32 error and div_rn introduces one more rounding, so the FP32 value can cross an FP16 tie boundary that the true real-value sigmoid does not, producing an off-by-one-ULP FP16 code. The FP16 output has only ~11 significant bits, so the FP32 margin around exact ties is small enough that 1-2 ulp FP32 error can flip the rounded result.", "scope": "in_scope", "scope_evidence": [{"source": "problem.txt", "summary": "Each output must be the real sigmoid value rounded ONCE to binary16 with round-to-nearest-even, exact bit patterns required for the whole public domain; one failing legal input is evidence against the implementation."}], "scope_rationale": "The contract requires the exact FP16 bit pattern of the single-rounded real sigmoid value for every finite FP16 input; a legal input (e.g., an x whose true sigmoid lies exactly or nearly halfway between two FP16 codes) where the kernel returns the neighboring code violates this stated rounding rule.", "statement": "There exist finite FP16 inputs x whose true sigmoid(x) lies at or extremely near a half-ULP boundary between two FP16 codes, where the kernel's FP32 intermediate (libdevice.exp error plus FP32 div) rounds to a different FP16 bit pattern than the required single rounding of the exact real value."}
function.name: record_claim

function.arguments: {"rationale": "The kernel relies on cvt.rn.f16.f32 without .ftz preserving subnormal RNE; if the PTX or the Triton-compiled SASS flushes subnormals or rounds them inconsistently with the FP64-then-'<e' packing used by reference(), subnormal outputs (e.g., for x ≈ -18.5 to -19) will mismatch. Also need to confirm output is +0 (not -0) for x < -24 where sigmoid underflows.", "scope": "in_scope", "scope_evidence": [{"source": "problem.txt", "summary": "Every finite FP16 encoding is legal including subnormals; positive sigmoid values that underflow binary16 round to positive zero; exact FP16 bit patterns must hold for the whole public domain."}], "scope_rationale": "The contract explicitly makes subnormal inputs legal, requires positive zero for underflowing sigmoid values, and requires exact FP16 bit patterns, so subnormal-output cases are directly in the stated domain.", "statement": "For strongly negative inputs (roughly x in [-24, -18], sigmoid outputs in the FP16 subnormal range down to positive zero), the kernel's e/(1+e) split form combined with cvt.rn.f16.f32 may produce a wrong subnormal bit pattern or a negative/flushed zero that mismatches the RNE-rounded FP64 reference."}

function.arguments: {"rationale": "For x around +17.3 to +19, sigmoid ≈ 1 - 2^-x sits just below FP16 codes like 0.9995; the split form computes 1/(1+e) in FP32 where the denominator rounds, which can differ by one FP16 ULP from the correctly rounded value. Also worth covering signed zeros and ±65504 explicitly and a tail N (e.g., 4093) that exercises the masked store.", "scope": "in_scope", "scope_evidence": [{"source": "problem.txt", "summary": "Both input zeros have mathematical output 0.5; the largest positive and negative finite values are legal; exact FP16 bit patterns and 1<=N<=131072 must hold for the whole public domain."}], "scope_rationale": "The contract explicitly names ±0 (output must be 0.5), ±65504, and the full N range [1,131072] as part of the public domain with exact-bit-pattern requirements, so these boundary inputs and non-multiple-of-BLOCK sizes are in scope.", "statement": "At extreme/edge inputs — x = ±0, ±65504, and x where sigmoid(x) rounds to exactly 1.0 or to the last subnormal code (the 1+e ≈ 1 cliff around |x| ≈ 17-18) — and at N not a multiple of 256 (e.g., N=4093), the kernel may return wrong bit patterns or mishandle masked tail lanes."}
function.name: record_claim

message.reasoning_content: Record claims: near-tie double rounding, subnormal underflow region, non-multiple-of-256 N tail / storage offset? Storage offset: kernel launches with x pointer — pointer arithmetic handles offsets fine. Focus: double-rounding near FP16 tie boundaries (in_scope), subnormal underflow region (in_scope), and large positive x clif (1+e rounds to 1 for x>~17.3, value=e exactly — matches reference since FP64 sigmoid ~ e too; low risk). Maybe record a third: cvt.rn.f16.f32 subnormal preservation vs struct '<e' — covered. Record 3 claims.
